text: Sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth!
Sing to the LORD, bless his name; proclaim his salvation day after day.
Declare his glory among the nations, his wonders among all peoples.
For great is the LORD, and worthy of all praise; he is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.
Ascribe to the LORD, you families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name; bring an offering and enter his courts.
Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness; tremble before him, all the earth.
Say among the nations, "The LORD reigns! Indeed, the world stands firm and cannot be shaken; he will judge the peoples with fairness."

versions.text: Say among the nations, "The LORD reigns!" The world stands firm and cannot be shaken; he will judge the peoples with justice.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew אַף ("indeed/surely") is untranslated, and the whole statement is naturally part of the quoted proclamation to the nations. Also בְּמֵישָׁרִים means "with equity/fairness/uprightness" — distinct from מִשְׁפָּט; "fairness" or "equity" is more precise than "justice."

text: Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad; let the sea and all that fills it resound.
Let the field exult, and everything in it; then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy

versions.text: Let the fields exult, and everything in them; then let all the trees of the forest sing for joy
versions.explanation: The verse ends without punctuation; since it runs on into verse 13, that is acceptable, but the Hebrew שָׂדַי is singular ("field") with a singular suffix ("in it"), and אָז יְרַנְּנוּ is naturally rendered as a future/consequence ("then... will sing") rather than a second jussive.

text: before the LORD, for he is coming—he is coming to judge the earth. He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples in his faithfulness.
